newsitem.title: UK: Chestertons drops 41 pct on profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Chestertons drops 41 pct on profit warning.

text.p: Shares in property consultancy Chesterton International Plc plummeted on Tuesday after the company warned profits in the past year would fall well below analysts' expectations.
The shares were down 23-1/2p or 41 percent to 33-1/2 by 1529 GMT in modest trade of 536,199 shares.

"Preliminary indications of the group's results for the year ended June 30 show that they will fall substantially below market expectations and may result in a loss for the year," the company said in a statement.
"In addition it is unlikely that a final dividend will be paid to shareholders."

Chief executive Michael Holmes said the results had been influenced by a number of factors including disappointing final quarter trading, certain one-off costs and the adoption of more prudent accounting policies.
"Since joining the company in April, I have reviewed each of the businesses in detail and have a clear view of their roles within our overall strategy," Holmes said.
"The focus of senior and middle management has been redirected, in some cases freeing senior professionals to devote more time to important fee generating work."
"I believe that the fundamentals of our business are sound and I am confident of Chesterton's prospects for the current year and beyond."
